Low-energy ball milling was conducted employing an omni-directional ball mill, equipped with vacuum-sealed stainless steel milling jars (100 mL) and ZrO2 grinding balls (d = 5 mm). All milling operations were carried out for 8 h at 120 r/min while maintaining a 4:1 ball-to-material ratio. To prevent oxidation, powder weighing and jar encapsulation were carried out in an argon-protected glove box.
Sintering was conducted at 1425 °C for 30 min at 50 MPa pressure.

evidence.section: 3.2 Microstructure of the sintered TiAl alloy and its composites
evidence.quote: A fully lamellar (FL) microstructure, mainly formed by α2/γ lamellar colonies, was observed in the as-sintered high Nb-TiAl alloy (Fig. 2 (a)). Its lamellar colony interfaces were characterized by straight and jagged interlocking patterns (Fig. 2 (b)). The lamellar colony size was approximately 235.6 μm (Fig. 2 (c)).

evidence.section: 3.2 Microstructure of the sintered TiAl alloy and its composites
evidence.quote: The 0.1SiB6/TiAl composite primarily contained α2/γ lamellar colonies. Discontinuous, network-distributed precipitates are found along the lamellar colony boundaries.

evidence.section: 4.5 Compositing inhibits high-temperature softening and enhances high-temperature strength
evidence.quote: Dynamic recrystallization serves as a key mechanism responsible for the softening of TiAl alloys at high temperatures, significantly influencing their high-temperature mechanical properties [76]. The mechanism of dynamic recrystallization is grain boundary migration controlled by atomic diffusion [68].
